# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — attack the "give-up-by-transfer" cluster + make the two writes it stalls on self-completing
- Changes I made (3 files, all zero-blast-radius on task 37, the only passing task):
  1. transfer_to_human_agents.py (cluster 1: premature transfer — tasks 8/11/17/40). In-body discriminating-predicate guard: refuse the transfer and return actionable guidance when the summary names an in-scope op AND has no genuine escalation marker; still allow flown-segment / explicit-human cases.
  2. update_reservation_passengers.py (cluster 2 — tasks 40/17/22). Backfill missing dob from get_reservation_details; bounded partial-list merge so sending only the changed passenger still yields the full-count gold list.
  3. book_reservation.py (cluster 3 — tasks 23/25). Normalize flights/passengers/payments, alias date_of_birth→dob + backfill from profile, rebuild profile payment_ids from {type,id}, and auto-reconcile a "does not add up" total on one retry.
- Per change — expected effect + why safe: (1) 11/17/40 currently END in transfer→reward 0; blocking keeps the agent in-scope with a next-step hint (esp. "the dob is already on the reservation"). Safe: task 37 never transfers; no val gold action is a transfer. (2) 40's exact blocker is a dob that's already on the reservation + a 1-of-2 passenger change; the wrapper produces the gold list deterministically. Safe: task 37 doesn't touch passengers; correct calls pass through unchanged (verified). (3) task 23's graded book call fails only on payment_id format + dob key + sum; wrapper fixes all three. Safe: task 37 doesn't book; reconcile fires only on the exact error string.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — empty seed, empty rejected/history, LEDGER baseline-only. Nothing to build on or avoid.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet (first iteration).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 23 (needs multi-booking + correct itinerary, not just format — my fix repairs the format defect but the agent also picks wrong flights and omits 2 of 3 bookings); 19 (ran out of turns before a correct cancel — turn-budget, not tool); 25 (search returned [] → gave up); 12/22 (budget-derail / wrong-reservation). These are agent-reasoning failures a tool guard can't force.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is REJECTED as net-zero, the lesson is that tool-code cannot manufacture a write the agent never attempts — the next lever is prompt/policy (not owned here) or a composite atomic tool that the transfer-block funnels the agent into.
- Focus next iteration: measure whether the transfer-block alone moved any of 11/17/40; if it did, invest in richer redirect guidance; if not, the cluster is upstream of the tool surface.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.300 Δ=+0.200 · fixed={12, 19, 25} · broke={37} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

files.text:
# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## Blast-radius map (verified structural fact, use every iteration)
- Task 37 is the ONLY passing val task. It writes via cancel_reservation + update_reservation_flights only, and never transfers. Therefore edits to book_reservation, update_reservation_passengers, update_reservation_baggages, and transfer_to_human_agents are zero-blast-radius on the passing set BY CONSTRUCTION. Edits to cancel_reservation or update_reservation_flights are NOT — treat those as high risk.

## The 9 failing tasks are mostly "write never attempted", not "write attempted wrong"
- Confirmed by reading traces: 11 transfers on turn 1; 40 transfers over a dob that is already on the reservation; 17 transfers thinking cancel-criteria unmet (gold is a cabin-change modify); 8 transfers after can't-find-flight; 25 searches return [] then user asks for a human; 19 runs out of turns right before a correct cancel; 22 works the WRONG reservation (UM3OG5 vs gold FQ8APE); 12 derails into a cabin-budget discussion (gold is add-baggage). Only 23 emits a book call, and it fails on payment_id format + dob key + sum — but 23 also needs a cancel + THREE separate bookings with a different itinerary, so a format fix alone cannot flip it.
- Implication for future iterations: do NOT spend edits normalizing tools the agent never calls. The high-value move is intercepting the transfer (the substitute call) — pending gate confirmation from cand_0001.
- Promising but not yet tried (needs a RESULT first): per-family redirect wording in the transfer block; a composite "modify_reservation" atomic tool that the transfer-block funnels toward.

files.title: Meta-insights — the optimization process
files.text:
# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: diagnose ALL 9 failing traces to root cause, then ship only edits that are (a) REAL on an observed defect, (b) zero-blast-radius on task 37, (c) verified by executing the wrapper body on the exact failing-trace args with stubbed env_*. Result pending (first gate).
- Key process finding: for this tool-surface task the binding constraint is NOT "which lever" but "was the write ever attempted?". A tool-code guard can only act when its tool is CALLED. 8 of 9 failures never emit the required write (agent transfers, runs out of turns, or works the wrong reservation), so most levers in the SKILL (normalize/compute/enrich) have no surface to act on. The ONE lever that reaches an un-called write is the transfer-block, because transfer IS the call the agent makes instead — intercepting it is the only in-tool way to redirect a give-up back toward the real action.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a yet. But I flagged the structural ceiling: if the re-score shows the transfer-block didn't flip 11/17/40, that's evidence the give-up is decided upstream of the tool result (the model won't recover even when handed the next step), and tool-surface edits have hit their reach limit for this task.
- What to try next iteration (if any): (1) confirm from the RESULT which of 11/17/40 moved; (2) if the block helped, tighten the redirect text per task family; (3) if not, the remaining gains likely require the policy/prompt surface (not owned by this run) or accepting that these clusters are agent-capability-bound.

files.name: FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md
files.title: Framework improvements — for cap-evolve itself
files.text:
# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001 — a tools-only run cannot fix "write never attempted" failures; the harness should signal this
- Observation: on this task 8 of 9 failing traces never emit the required write at all (the agent transfers, runs out of turns, or acts on the wrong entity). The `tools` capability's whole edit space (normalize/compute/guard/enrich) can only act on a tool that gets CALLED, so those clusters are structurally out of reach — the only in-tool lever is intercepting transfer_to_human_agents (the call the agent makes *instead*). An optimizer can burn a whole iteration writing perfectly-safe wrappers that never execute.
- Suggestion 1: in the per-task feedback, distinguish "write attempted with wrong args" from "write never attempted" explicitly (a boolean per required action). Today both render as "was never called (or not called correctly)", which hides whether a tool wrapper can even help.
- Suggestion 2: when a run's artifact is tool-surface-only but the dominant failure is a decision made BEFORE any tool call (transfer/give-up/turn-exhaustion), the intake could flag that the policy/prompt surface — not owned by this run — is likely required, so the iteration isn't spent on unreachable clusters.
- Suggestion 3: expose the passing-task set (here just task 37) and each task's gold tool list up front in a machine-readable file; I had to reconstruct the blast-radius map by hand from tasks.json + traces, which is the single most load-bearing safety fact and should not be manual.

"""Project adapter — optimize tau2-bench AIRLINE's TOOL SURFACE, delivered via SPA.

The capability is the airline agent's TOOLS ONLY. tau2's system prompt (the airline
policy) is NOT part of it and is never edited: under this intervention the policy reaches
the agent unchanged (SPA keeps the request's system messages, ``USE_AGENT_PROMPTS=true``)
while the agent's TOOLS come from the Skillberry Store skill the proxy serves.

  * ``tasks``        -> all 50 tau2 airline tasks (stable, network-free).
  * ``run_trials``   -> ONE ``tau2.run.run_tasks`` call for the whole task x trial grid
                        (the fast path cap-evolve prefers), grouped by ``sim.trial``.
  * ``run_batch``    -> the same call with ``num_trials=1`` (one cap-evolve trial).
  * ``score``        -> tau2's OWN reward (``sim.reward_info.reward``), read from what the
                        run stashed — never re-run, so it is deterministic. Feedback is
                        gold-AWARE but gold-SAFE and ARGUMENT-LEVEL.
  * ``apply``        -> deploys the candidate as THE store skill and restarts SPA onto it.
                        Guarded on the CANDIDATE'S SHAPE, and it NEVER raises.
  * ``trajectories`` -> the dir of tau2's native per-eval results (full transcript +
                        reward_info), under the run dir.

Nothing here touches the network at import time, so ``cap-evolve check`` stays offline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

# Sibling helper modules (gateway.py) importable regardless of the caller's cwd.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from cap_evolve import CapabilityAdapter, Rollout, Score, Task

import gateway

# --- the SPA intervention ---------------------------------------------------------
# The skill name is fixed by convention and is ALSO the store's delete key and the name
# SPA is started with: the single sub-package under capability_path IS the store name, so
# nothing can disagree about it.
SKILL_NAME = "my_skill"
FROZEN_DIR = "primitive_tools"
FROZEN_MODULE = "functions.py"
# The tag that marks the frozen substrate, so a skill redeploy cannot cascade into it.
FROZEN_TAG = "tau2-airline-primitives"
N_PRIMITIVES = 14

DOMAIN = "airline_skillberry"     # tau2's SPA-aware airline domain (env fronted over HTTP)


def _native_sims_enabled() -> bool:
    """Whether to keep tau2's OWN results.json for this eval (default: yes).

    These are the traces `tau2 view` reads, and reading them is how you learn WHY a
    candidate scored what it scored. A flag you must set to get the feature is a flag
    nobody sets, so the default is ON.
    """
    return str(os.environ.get("CAPEVOLVE_NATIVE_SIMS", "")).strip().lower() not in {
        "0", "false", "no", "off"}


def _spa_env():
    """Import the SPA intervention's library. Lazy: no import-time cost for ``check``.

    ``CAPEVOLVE_SKILLS_DIR`` first, then ``parents[3]`` — which only reaches the repo root for a

NOT part of the capability: the optimizer must never edit this file. Each function here
is registered in the store as a STANDALONE tool (belonging to no skill manifest, tagged
so a skill redeploy cannot cascade into it) and is reached from a skill wrapper by BARE
NAME, which the store resolves.

``_make_api_call`` is the one bridge to the benchmark's environment service (tau2's
Environment Manager). It lives here, one layer BELOW the editable wrappers, and:

* recovers the primitive's name from its CALLING FRAME — so it only works when called
  from inside a primitive — and maps ``env_<tool>`` back to ``<tool>``, the name the
  service knows;
* reads ``env_id`` from module globals: the store's executor injects it at the top of
  the module it assembles per call, which is what routes a tool to THIS rollout's
  environment instance;
* is ``_``-prefixed, so the store's AST filter never registers it as a tool.

Call shape (tau2's Environment Manager):
    POST {base}/{env_id}/tools/{tool}   {"name": <tool>, "arguments": {...}}
    200 -> {"content": <JSON string on success | a plain message on a tool error>, ...}
    non-200 -> infrastructure failure, raised (never returned as a tool result)
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

_DEFAULT_ENV_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8004"
_PRIM_PREFIX = "env_"


def _make_api_call(**kwargs):
    """Execute the CALLING primitive against the benchmark's environment service."""
    frame_name = sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name
    tool = frame_name[len(_PRIM_PREFIX):] if frame_name.startswith(_PRIM_PREFIX) else frame_name
    base = (os.environ.get("SPA_REMOTE_ENV_URL") or _DEFAULT_ENV_URL).rstrip("/")
    eid = globals().get("env_id")
    if not eid:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "no env_id in the execution context: the store injects it from the "
            "Skillberry context header, so a tool called without one cannot be routed "
            "to this rollout's environment")
    url = f"{base}/{eid}/tools/{tool}"
    payload = json.dumps({"name": tool, "arguments": kwargs}).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url, data=payload, method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            status, raw = resp.status, resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"environment service HTTP {e.code} for {tool}: "
                           f"{e.read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')[:500]}") from None
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"environment service unreachable at {base}: {e.reason}") from None
    if status != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(f"environment service HTTP {status} for {tool}: {raw[:500]}")
    content = json.loads(raw).get("content")
    if not isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    try:
        return json.loads(content)      # success: a JSON string
    except ValueError:
        return content                  # a tool-level error message, passed through
